subject: General Knowledge
description: Indian classical instruments and their famous exponents

questions.stem: Pandit Ravi Shankar was a world-famous exponent of which instrument?
questions.explanation: Ravi Shankar (1920-2012) popularised the sitar worldwide and collaborated with George Harrison of the Beatles. He received the Bharat Ratna in 1999. Sarod is associated with the Ali Akbar Khan / Amjad Ali Khan tradition; santoor with Shivkumar Sharma; shehnai with Bismillah Khan.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Ustad Bismillah Khan was celebrated for his mastery of the:
questions.explanation: Bismillah Khan (1916-2006) made the shehnai — earlier a ceremonial wedding instrument — a classical concert instrument. He played on 15 August 1947 at the Red Fort and received the Bharat Ratna in 2001. Sarangi is a bowed string instrument; tabla was associated with Zakir Hussain (among others); bansuri with Hariprasad Chaurasia.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the instrument with its famous exponent. A. Sarod. B. Santoor. C. Bansuri. D. Tabla. List-II: 1. Shivkumar Sharma, 2. Amjad Ali Khan, 3. Zakir Hussain, 4. Hariprasad Chaurasia.
questions.explanation: Sarod — Amjad Ali Khan (also Ali Akbar Khan). Santoor — Shivkumar Sharma (brought the Kashmiri folk instrument into Hindustani classical). Bansuri (bamboo flute) — Hariprasad Chaurasia. Tabla — Zakir Hussain (son of Ustad Alla Rakha). All four received Padma honours.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: M. S. Subbulakshmi, the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna, was associated with which form of music?
questions.explanation: M. S. Subbulakshmi (1916-2004) was a leading Carnatic vocalist — Bharat Ratna (1998), Magsaysay Award (1974), famed for her 'Suprabhatam' and 'Vishnu Sahasranamam' renditions. She also performed at the UN General Assembly in 1966. Hindustani classical vocalists of similar stature include Bhimsen Joshi and Kumar Gandharva; qawwali is associated with Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan; thumri is a Hindustani semi-classical form.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Sarangi' is which type of instrument?
questions.explanation: Sarangi — a short-necked, bowed string instrument with sympathetic strings, long used to accompany khyal and thumri vocalists; tone is considered closest to the human voice. Famous exponents: Ram Narayan, Sultan Khan. Tabla is percussion; shehnai and bansuri are wind; sitar and sarod are plucked.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Mridangam', the principal percussion instrument of South Indian classical music, is a:
questions.explanation: Mridangam — a wooden barrel-shaped drum with leather heads on both sides, central to Carnatic music. 'Pair of hand drums' describes the tabla (Hindustani). The kettle-drum family (naqqara, timpani) is different. Legendary mridangam players: Palghat Mani Iyer, Umayalpuram Sivaraman, Palani Subramaniam Pillai.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Amjad Ali Khan, recipient of the Padma Vibhushan, is renowned for playing which instrument?
questions.explanation: Amjad Ali Khan belongs to a six-generation sarod lineage — his father Hafiz Ali Khan was a leading exponent. Sarod — fretless plucked string instrument with a metal fingerboard. The Ali Akbar Khan / Maihar gharana is the other great sarod tradition. Sitar has frets (Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan); surbahar is a bass sitar; veena is a South Indian plucked string instrument.
